# Alerting and Detection Strategy (ADS) — Rule 100013

## Goal

What adversary behavior this detection is meant to catch. Name the ATT&CK technique(s).

## Categorization

- **ATT&CK technique(s):** `T1105` — Ingress Tool Transfer
- **Tactic(s) (v20):** Command and Control
- **Lab rule_id:** `100013`
- **Source Sigma rule:** `rules/sigma/T1105_certutil_urlcache.yml`

## Strategy Abstract

How the detection works, in plain language: which telemetry field(s), what condition, what it keys on.

## Technical Context

The concrete detail a reviewer needs to judge the rule: the exact Sysmon event, the fields used, the Wazuh decoder/field names (`win.eventdata.commandLine`, `win.eventdata.image`, ...), and how the Sigma `logsource` maps onto them.

```xml
<!-- Rule 100013 - Certutil URL download (urlcache) -->
<!-- MITRE ATT&CK: T1105 - Ingress Tool Transfer -->
<!-- Sysmon Event ID 1 - Process Creation -->
<!-- Hand written from rules/sigma/T1105_certutil_urlcache.yml (sigma_to_wazuh skips multi-selection conditions). -->
<rule id="100013" level="8">
  <if_sid>61603</if_sid>
  <field name="win.eventdata.originalFileName" type="pcre2">(?i)^certutil\.exe$</field>
  <field name="win.eventdata.commandLine" type="pcre2">(?i)urlcache</field>
  <description>T1105: Certutil URL download - $(win.eventdata.commandLine)</description>
  <mitre>
    <id>T1105</id>
  </mitre>
</rule>
```

## Blind Spots and Assumptions

Microsoft Defender RTP needed to be disabled first for the rule to be tested. For the atomic test to be ran offline, the file was pointed against the local HTTP server.

## False Positives

What benign activity could trigger this, and what the baseline measurement actually showed. Reference the baseline manifest action if an FP was seen.

## Validation

- **Positive test:** which atomic test GUID fires it, and the result (detected Y/N, latency).
- **Converter fidelity (if converted from Sigma):** `wazuh-logtest` output confirms the converted rule matches a crafted event
- **Negative test:** the 5-run baseline FP cost.

## Priority / Response

Suggested alert level and a one-line analyst response.
